    Summary

    Jimsa brings two orphaned wolf pups to the only man in Peshawar who might know what to do with them.

    Isfān agrees to train the wolves temporarily. Jimsa returns with meat temporarily. The wolves acquire names, collars, household colours and an increasingly settled place in Isfān’s quarters, while Jimsa keeps finding practical reasons to come back and Isfān keeps finding no practical reason to object.

    Then Kubard gives Isfān a title.

    By the following morning, half of Peshawar has apparently decided it explains everything.

    As rumours about the Mother of Wolves spread, Jimsa learns that asking for the truth does not entitle him to it, the wolves begin deciding for themselves who belongs near them, and Isfān discovers that trusting someone in practice is considerably easier than deciding what that trust means.

    Shapur, meanwhile, has noticed all of this.

    He concludes that Isfān's future requires organisation.

    The wolves disagree with nearly everyone's assessment of the situation.

    Summary

    In this alternate timeline, Shapur survived the Battle of Atropatene, Kubard survived the reclaiming of Ecbatana, and Arslan ascended the throne. Isfān never suffers the eye injury he receives in canon, while Jimsa chooses to remain in Arslan’s service after the war.

    With Ecbatana still recovering from the Lusitanian occupation, parts of the army have been dispersed among the roads and border fortresses rather than returned to the capital all at once. Peshawar’s swollen garrison has consequently become an unlikely meeting place for commanders, soldiers and households whose lives might otherwise have remained separate.

    When Jimsa sets out from Peshawar to hunt, he expects to return with meat and little else. Instead, two orphaned wolf pups follow him back to the fortress. They lead him to Isfān. Over the following weeks, Jimsa becomes part of their care, Isfān begins treating the wolves as his own while insisting they remain temporary, and Shapur returns to find that his household has changed considerably in his absence.

    The wolves are temporary, Isfān is certain.
    No one else seems convinced.

    Summary

    The gates of the Royal Capital, Ecbatana, rose ahead. The Lusitanian army advanced towards them, smoke still clinging to their banners from the villages they had put to the torch along the way.

    At the front of their march stood a single wooden post. A man was bound to it, chains biting into torn flesh, blood pooling at his feet. He stood upright — head high, gaze unbroken. When he spoke, his voice carried across the plain. "People of Ecbatana — shoot me. Better to die by a friend's arrow than by the hands of these savages."
    Only then did his name matter. Marzbān Shapur.

    High above, upon the city wall, a hooded woman watched. Cold stone pressed through her gloves as the wind tugged at her cloak. She did not move when the moment came.

    The arrow was swift. Merciful.
    A single tear slipped down her cheek — the last she would ever shed for the old Kingdom of Pars.

    In the days that followed, the fall of Ecbatana would draw her back into the path of a young prince who refused to accept the world as it stood. The kingdom that had cast her aside would demand her return — and test what she still believed in.
    And if the gods were kind, the ruins might yet give rise to something worth saving.

    Summary

    Twenty-four doors. Three Spirits. Two letters. One rather stubborn Christmas elf.

    Join our beloved Lusitanian Etoile on an unexpected journey through mysterious encounters that challenge her to look at the world — and herself — through different eyes.

    Inspired by Charles Dickens's A Christmas Carol and set in the world of Yoshiki Tanaka's Arslan Senki and Hiromu Arakawa's manga adaptation, this Advent calendar unfolds through two letters addressed to Etoile's grandfather, exploring prejudice, compassion, the consequences of our choices and the possibility of change.

    A collaborative project between KayleySayer and cradium, first begun in 2017 and finally brought to completion in 2025.

    The illustrated version of this Advent calendar can be found on Tumblr.

    A nameless girl had been living her life peacefully, hidden from the outside world – and hidden from the Order Coffin Company – until the night she stumbled into a battle between vampires and Kownloon Children. In the chaos, she was gravely wounded, and darkness claimed her.

    Believing her to be a vampire, a Company investigation team brought her to the Special Zone, placing her fate in the hands of the “Dragon King of the East,” Sei.

    Sei, against the protests of others - particularly Zelman Clock - allowed her to remain in the Special Zone under Zelman’s care. Something in her stirred his curiosity: a desperate, unyielding grip on fragments of a past even she seemed not to understand.

    Her aura was fragile, but there was a quiet strength in her. Sei wanted to protect her, to win her trust. But he knew well that safety in the Special Zone was fragile - bought with ceaseless struggle and sacrifice.

    What no one yet realised was that she might be the one foretold to end their endless war.
